title: Special-Order Part Release on Repair and Emergency Service Calls
content:
When an approved repair on a call under Repair and Emergency Service Calls waits for a special-order part, the part is released for order on the customer's release payment, made in person. The payment is recorded as a payment line on the call's invoice and lowers the balance owing on that call.

## Conditions on taking the payment

> The special-order deposit payment is taken only after the after-hours premium line on a member's call carries the member premium discount line owed on it.

> No special-order deposit payment is taken until the paid tune-up line of a courtesy-program customer's call carries the courtesy discount line owed on it.

## Payment tool: `pay_special_order_deposit_ccffba41`

**What it does.** The customer pays, in person through the secure payment line, the amount required to release a special-order part on one of their own service calls. Each run of the tool records one payment line on the call's invoice, dated today, with a newly issued payment confirmation number. It lowers the call's invoice balance by exactly the amount paid. The customer hears the confirmation number at once, and the payment shows among the call's invoice lines. The tool does not check eligibility or amounts; it books what it is given.

**How it is invoked.** This is a hidden customer-side tool. The agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it by the name `pay_special_order_deposit_ccffba41`; the payment is made by the customer in person.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format and values |
|---|---|---|
| `ticket_id` | Reference number of the service call the special-order part was quoted on, as the agent reads it from the service call lookup and gives it to the customer | Id |
| `amount` | The payment amount | USD, 2 decimal places, always positive; a value with more decimals is rounded to the cent half up when booked |
| `payment_method` | How the customer pays | One of `card` (debit or credit card), `ach` (from a checking or savings account by bank transfer), `check` (a mailed or handed-over paper check), `cash` (cash at the office) |

**Return.** The tool returns a receipt with `line_id` (reference number of the payment line), `ticket_id`, `amount` (USD to 2 decimal places), `payment_method` (as passed), `payment_reference` (the confirmation number issued for this payment), `posted_date` (YYYY-MM-DD) and `ticket_balance` (the call's invoice balance in USD after the payment). A receipt carrying a `payment_reference` means the payment was taken.
